newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Stanbic says can live with hit from NAB.
newsitem.headline: Stanbic says can live with hit from NAB.

text.p: Standard Bank Investment Corp Ltd, owed 230 million rand by ailing Pepsi bottler New Age Beverages (NAB), is facing potentially its biggest bad debt loss to date.
But the group's merchant bank arm said on Monday it could take the loss without any significant impact on future group earnings.

"It's clearly going to be a substantial loss, but we don't believe it is going to have a material negative impact of earnings for Standard Bank Group," said Standard Corporate and Merchant Bank (SCMB) managing director Jacko Maree.
Shares in the banking group fell sharply on Monday, closing down 775 cents at 205.00 rand as investors took fright at the fact that SCMB was the major creditor to NAB.
"We've got an exposure to New Age of 230 million (rand), a reasonable amount of money. How much we are going to get back out of the liquidation procedures is an open question," Maree said.
NAB applied for voluntary liquidation on Friday, just three years after it spearheaded Pepsi's high-profile return to South Africa.
Industry sources said PepsiCo Inc may not have given up on South Africa, despite the problems at NAB, which could yet be resurrected in a different form.
Pepsi kicked off a South African division of the global cola wars three years ago, entering the market via NAB with its eyes fixed initially on black townships, such as Soweto outside Johannesburg.
More recently the battle has been widened to a countrywide showdown between Pepsi and arch-rival Coca-Cola Co.
Coke and its seven bottlers upped the stakes earlier this year with ambitious plans for a one billion rand investment in South Africa.
